stance_summary: NO TRADE. The Sep-16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% and the Sep-17 official SOFR print of 3.85% are delivered; SR3 already prices +15bp (SR3U6 4.00) to +90.5bp (SR3U7 4.755) versus that overnight fixing, so both paying and receiving the US strip are either late or fighting still-hot US gauges (inflation 72, labor 75). Canada looks like the closest discrepancy—CORRA 2.29 versus CRAH27 3.13 (+84bp) and CRAM28 3.65 (+136bp) with labor 38 and headline CPI 3%/core near 2%—but CA 2Y 3.27 is already the 97.8th one-year percentile after +31bp in one month, CA-US 2Y -140bp sits at the 3.8th one-year / 4.3rd five-year percentile, BoC minutes already flag energy pass-through, one-month CORRA is only +14bp by November, and the paper book is two-way in CORRA_2027-03. Australia prices ~21.5-59bp of AONIA hikes while inflation is 82 and housing is already biting; that is a two-sided narrative, not a residual. AUDCAD/AUDNZD at the 99.8-100th percentile are discovery screens, not theses, and carry plus AU-CA 2Y ~165bp can keep them there. NZ sovereign yields and NZ policy path are unavailable, CFTC TFF is dated 2026-09-15 (pre-FOMC), CME positioning is unavailable, STIR open interest is mostly null, FX marks are 2026-09-18 versus a Sunday cutoff, and options lack premium/IV. The book is FLAT and last cycle earned official SOFR cash; that 3.85% ACT/360 hurdle (~$10,694 per calendar day on $100m) is still the cleaner expression than buying a priced post-event debate.

rejected_expression_comparison.rationale: Rates would be preferred over spot if either candidate were actionable. Neither is: the CORRA receive is priced, two-way crowded, and contradicted by BoC energy-pass-through minutes plus CA 2Y already at the 97.8th one-year percentile; AUDCAD is a statistical extreme without a weakening mechanism, with AU inflation 82, housing-channel tightening already known, and CFTC AUD open interest at a one-year extreme. Cash at official SOFR 3.85% ACT/360 is the expression that does not require inventing an unpriced discrepancy from stale or missing marks.

what_would_make_actionable: A live, unpriced catalyst after the delivered Sep-16 hike; NZ rates and NZ policy path restored so AU-NZ or NZ duration can be tested; post-event positioning (CFTC after 2026-09-16 and/or CME or CORRA/SR3 open interest) showing one-sided ownership against a still-mispriced path; or a rates expression whose expected edge, after carry and the official 3.85% ACT/360 cash hurdle, has a packet-sourced invalidation and is not already two-way in the paper book. A SOFR fixing sustainably above the 4.00 band while SR3Z6 remained 4.32 would reopen a US funding/path discrepancy; a BoC communication that explicitly rejects the +84bp by Mar-27 while CRAH27 failed to cheapen would reopen Canada. Percentile extremes alone would not.

context_build.causal_mechanism: The room is testing whether a delivered global tightening impulse (Fed 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, BoJ 25bp to 1.25%, energy-shock constraint on easing) has left a residual in G10 policy paths or FX that is not already in SR3/CORRA/AONIA strips and sovereign percentiles. The skeptic's mechanism is the opposite: once a >90%-priced hike is delivered and overnight SOFR has jumped 23bp to 3.85%, remaining term-premium/hike odds are the priced path, not an edge, and cash compounding at the official fixing dominates fading or chasing that path.

context_build.market_implied_assumption: US: additional hikes of about 47bp by Dec-26 (SR3Z6 4.32) and about 73-90.5bp by Mar-Sep 2027, with the strip peaking near 4.755 then modestly reversing. Canada: almost no hike by Oct, +14bp by Nov, then a full cycle to 3.13 by Mar-27 and ~3.65 by 2028. Australia: roughly one 25bp move into Oct and a second by late 2026, then a slower grind toward 4.94 by mid-2027. FX: AUD near parity versus CAD and historically rich versus NZD is consistent with that AU-CA policy gap remaining wide.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The skeptic does not claim the priced hike paths are 'wrong' in a tradable way. The disagreed assumption is the room's implicit claim that a percentile extreme or a labor-versus-strip gap after a delivered, pre-priced hike is still an edge that clears official SOFR cash. That assumption is what NO TRADE rejects.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end US/CA/AU trades would have live policy paths, and those paths already embed the hike cycles other seats want to pay or receive. That availability is why NO TRADE is not a data blackout on US/CA/AU; it is a judgment that the paths are priced. NZ cannot support a rates-first expression. A 2Y sovereign percentile is not a substitute for those strips, and the strips do not leave an unpriced residual that clears official SOFR cash.
